themes_detail.label: Tree Overgrowth Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked to 14 THIS WEEK, up 250% from the 4-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.47), suggesting either a weather event, deferred maintenance surge, or safety hazard concentrated in this neighborhood.
evidence: 14 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Complaint volume represents 3.5x baseline rate, suggesting acute, district-wide issue rather than isolated incident
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about maintenance backlog or resource allocation in CD 314
Canvass affected blocks (Midwood, Ocean Parkway areas) to document which trees pose safety hazards and whether residents fear falling branches

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Missing and damaged street signs combined represent 12 complaints THIS WEEK (6 missing + 6 damaged), up 384% and 433% respectively from weekly baselines, indicating rapid deterioration of wayfinding and traffic-control infrastructure across the district.
evidence: 6 missing street signs THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (336% spike, z-score: 4.66)
6 damaged street signs THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (433% spike, z-score: 3.84)
Combined 12-complaint spike suggests systemic failure in maintenance or vandalism pattern
reporting_angles: Map the affected intersections to identify whether damage is concentrated in one area or scattered
Contact DOT about maintenance priorities and whether Midwood/Ocean Parkway area has been deprioritized

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints exploded to 5 LAST WEEK, up 900% from the 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.36), the highest-severity spike in the dataset, suggesting either a bike-share or private bike abandonment crisis.
evidence: 5 abandoned bike complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
900% spike with z-score of 6.36 (highest statistical severity in dataset)
Suggests acute event (e.g., bike-share rebalancing failure, theft spike, or dumping campaign)
reporting_angles: Check whether Citi Bike or other bike-share operator has had service disruptions or rebalancing issues in Midwood
Interview sanitation workers and local residents about where bikes are accumulating and condition (locked, damaged, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Garbage Container Shortage
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests jumped to 4 complaints THIS WEEK, up 191% from the 1.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42), indicating residents perceive insufficient public trash receptacles in the district.
evidence: 4 litter basket requests THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Suggests either Sanitation removal of receptacles, or new density/foot traffic straining existing capacity
reporting_angles: Check with Sanitation Department on whether baskets were removed from CD 314 recently or if budget cuts reduced deployment
Identify the specific blocks with complaints to assess whether issue is concentrated near transit hubs, parks, or commercial zones

themes_detail.label: Seasonal Heat Complaints Plummet
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints dropped 84% THIS WEEK to 39, down from 246.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: -4.21), indicating either seasonal warming or widespread complaint resolution, but warrants verification that the decline reflects actual repairs rather than seasonal demand drop.
evidence: 39 heat/hot water complaints THIS WEEK vs. 246.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Timing suggests seasonal shift rather than enforcement action, but unusual magnitude warrants investigation
reporting_angles: Verify whether decline is seasonal (warmer weather = less heating demand) or reflects actual repair rate improvement
Cross-reference with HPD violation data to see if landlords have been cited or if backlog of complaints has been cleared
